doc.name: A — outerwear catalogue, sunbeam blinds, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: double-face wool coat
Category: outerwear
Shot programme: sunbeam blinds
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are a commercial stills director briefing an outerwear capture. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the split-level stack in a sunbeam blinds treatment.

SUBJECT. A double-face wool coat. Copy the product from the reference verbatim in form and finish. If a detail is unreadable in the reference, keep it neutral rather than inventing one.

CAMERA. Product on a stepped plinth arrangement at two heights. Shoot on a 50mm normal at f/1.2, framing for a tight crop that breaks the subject at the frame edge.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with split gel lighting, teal on the shadow side and magenta on the key side. Stage the product on or against matte acrylic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a punchy saturated candy palette with hard primaries. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
